newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - June 27.

text.p: Spendthrifts buckle bottom line: Presented as a package containing a mix of economic growth promotants and spending initiatives already promised, the Budget will disappoint significant constituents on both counts. Page 1.

Apple cartel squeezes growers: Facing cashflows $20 million lower than the same time last year, slow sales, low prices and "reasonably significant" stockpiles of fruit, the Apple & Pear Board this week deferred its progress payments to growers. Page 1.

Skellerup sells its mining arm: Skellerup Group subsidiary DML Resources has sold its mining business -- the company formerly known as L & M Mining -- and all but one of its quarries, DML chief executive Stuart Walbridge says. Page 3.

SFO extends ACC probe to Aussie: The Serious Fraud Office inquiry into former ACC boss Gavin Robins has expanded to several Australian companies, including Victoria-based Compensation Systems. Page 3.

NZ Insurance defies industry defies industry downturn: NZ Insurance's 1996 results, published on Thursday, show the company continues to keep its place as one of the few fire and general insurers turning a profit. Page 3.
Air NZ continues to defy ACC: Air New Zealand and the Accident Compensation Corporation have agreed to take their dispute about employer levies back to the discussion table. Page 3.
Winebox wind-up to begin: The winebox inquiry enters its final stages on Tuesday, with the parties presenting oral submissions to commissioner Sir Ron Davison. Page 4.

Singapore open skies pact will bolster Air NZ, SIA, Ansett alliance: An open skies agreement with Singapore now being finalised will bolster the recently forged alliance between Air New Zealand, Ansett Australia and Singapore Airlines. Page 6.
Further breakup of ECNZ on the cards: ECNZ appears to be broken up further -- into several competing state-owned electricity generators. Page 1.

Absence of court reform hurts business: The New Zealand courts are one of the last areas of unreformed work practices and are imposing unwarranted extra costs on businesses, Commerce Commission chairman Alan Bollard says. Page 1.
Farming nations snub NZ: The New Zealand government is watching with concern an apparent European Union move to shut it out of a meeting of top farming countries in Paris next year. Page 1.

Police tender process cleared despite concern over burglary: Sensitive computer files were stolen from the offices of Tandem Computing, a bidder for the controversial Card 111 emergency system contract, as the tender process was being completed. Page 3.

Southern householders trial choosing utilities: Christchurch power supplier Southpower and Dunedin supplier United will seek Commerce Commission approval for the country's first trial programme aimed at introducing power competition for householders. Page 3.
Home in Sky for Chisholm: Expatriate millionaire Sam Chisholm, of BSkyB fame could be headed back home as the chairman of an Independent Newspapers Ltd-owned Sky Network Television. Page 4.
New plant boost for South: Rayonier New Zealand's official opening of its $180 million medium density fibre-board plant at Mataura should prove a shot in the arm for the Southland economy. Page 9.

Digital network off the ground soon: Phase one of Broadcast Communications' digital distribution network (DDN) could be operational in as little as two or three months' time, according to the BCL general manager of networks, Rob Sweet. Page 9.
